# Find the inference bottleneck first: weights, KV content, or cache tiers

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/foundation-models/compression-and-cache.md) · English

Updated 2026-10-30 · 32 topic entries / 9 representative comparisons

AWQ reduces weight bit width; GQA shares KV heads; DropKV and TwinKV change retained content; KVMEM manages executable history views; Remote KV Tiers decides cross-tier loading. They can combine, but one compression ratio cannot explain quality, recoverability, and end-to-end speed. FoldBias makes compressed caches compatible with standard interfaces by folding static bias into equal-width keys, while future query drift still causes error.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Four kinds of capacity reductions

AWQ stores the same weights in fewer bytes, GQA lowers KV heads per token, DropKV removes positions, and TwinKV reallocates a fixed position budget. The first two need not reduce history length and the latter two do not compress weights. AWQ can free room without changing long-output KV growth, while eviction may not fix weight-read bottlenecks.

Sources: [AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration](../../../../reproductions/2306.00978-awq/README-en.md) · [GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints](../../../../reproductions/2305.13245-gqa/README-en.md) · [DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction](../../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en.md) · [TwinKV: A Composable Repair Pass for KV Cache Eviction via Pairwise Key Redundancy](../../../../reproductions/2608.27128-twinkv/README-en.md)

### Deletion versus movement changes future access

DropKV and TwinKV constrain visible history to what is retained. KVMEM separates the large address space from the small execution view; unselected blocks can remain in backing storage. Remote KV Tiers asks whether fixed load overhead plus bytes divided by bandwidth beats recomputation. Hits, retained data, GPU memory, and speed are distinct evidence. Local KVMEM keeps full backing cache and no remote implementation was measured.

Sources: [DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction](../../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en.md) · [KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU](../../../../reproductions/2609.04852-kvmem/README-en.md) · [When the KV Cache Is Slower Than the GPU: Scaling Remote KV Tiers for Context-Parallel Prefill](../../../../foundation-models/2610.21500-remote-kv-tiers/README-en.md)

### October 29: new methods and scope changes

ResCom adds a low-rank branch to a fixed quantized host to read activation rounding residuals; calibration and intercept must match that host. HOPE uses Gaussian–ReLU/Hilbert proxies to prune structured neurons and compensate downstream means. These are not universally equivalent pruning/quantization combinations. Local exact small components do not reproduce LLM or ImageNet matrices.

Sources: [AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration](../../../../reproductions/2306.00978-awq/README-en.md) · [ResCom: Activation Residual Compensation for Large Language Model Quantization](../../../../foundation-models/2610.35955-rescom/README-en.md) · [Hilbert Operator for Progressive Encoding (HOPE): A Mathematical Framework for Deconstructing Learned Representations in Deep Networks](../../../../foundation-models/2607.21366-hope-hilbert/README-en.md)

### Standard cache compatibility does not eliminate compression error

GQA changes per-token KV storage by sharing heads. FoldBias preserves head width and query paths while folding an existing compression's static logit bias into `β(q·u)`, accurate only when query projection is near one. Refit values after key rounding to match actual kernel inputs. AM key selection, NNLS, and engine integration remain independent; small matrices do not prove throughput or full cache quality.

Sources: [Folding Attention Biases into Keys Makes Compacted KV Caches Run on Standard Kernels](../../../../foundation-models/2610.36520-fold-bias/README-en.md) · [GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints](../../../../reproductions/2305.13245-gqa/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Which memory growth terms do AWQ and GQA change in long conversations, and why might eviction still be needed? {#cross-weights-versus-history}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** AWQ lowers resident weight bytes. GQA lowers per-token KV bytes but history count still grows. DropKV-like selection can bound history count while risking information loss. Report the three quantities separately.

    **Illustrative example:** Thinner shelves do not reduce the arrival of books; GQA makes books smaller and eviction decides which books stay.

    Sources: [AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration](../../../../reproductions/2306.00978-awq/README-en.md) · [GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints](../../../../reproductions/2305.13245-gqa/README-en.md) · [DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction](../../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en.md)

### How do DropKV and TwinKV differ when two important KV entries are redundant? {#cross-importance-versus-substitution}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** DropKV estimates each entry's output impact from observed attention probabilities and values. TwinKV repairs a base set by swapping donors with substitutes for orphans without alternatives. They address individual importance and set coverage and can combine, but require quality and budget checks.

    **Illustrative example:** Two near-duplicate plan entries can be exchanged to recover the only authorization scope if key similarity really implies substitutability.

    Sources: [DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction](../../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en.md) · [TwinKV: A Composable Repair Pass for KV Cache Eviction via Pairwise Key Redundancy](../../../../reproductions/2608.27128-twinkv/README-en.md)

### Why might Remote KV Tiers recommend recomputation after KVMEM finds a block? {#cross-cache-hit-versus-recompute}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** An address makes reuse possible, not free. Low bandwidth, small blocks, or queueing can make `T0 + bytes/bandwidth` exceed a new prefill. Execution view limits visibility; the break-even rule decides how to retrieve. Hit rate alone cannot choose.

    **Illustrative example:** A remote hit on a short prefix may lose to local recomputation, while a long prefix amortizes fixed overhead.

    Sources: [KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU](../../../../reproductions/2609.04852-kvmem/README-en.md) · [When the KV Cache Is Slower Than the GPU: Scaling Remote KV Tiers for Context-Parallel Prefill](../../../../foundation-models/2610.21500-remote-kv-tiers/README-en.md)

### Why can't ResCom correction rank be read as the number of HOPE neurons that can be pruned? {#cross-oct29-method-boundary}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** ResCom budgets low-rank output-error compensation. HOPE costs depend on neuron Hilbert capacity and original parameter footprint. Their parameter locations, states, and calibration assumptions differ.

    **Illustrative example:** Keeping every quantized output plus a rank-two correction is not deleting two neurons and compensating the downstream mean.

    Sources: [AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration](../../../../reproductions/2306.00978-awq/README-en.md) · [ResCom: Activation Residual Compensation for Large Language Model Quantization](../../../../foundation-models/2610.35955-rescom/README-en.md) · [Hilbert Operator for Progressive Encoding (HOPE): A Mathematical Framework for Deconstructing Learned Representations in Deep Networks](../../../../foundation-models/2607.21366-hope-hilbert/README-en.md)

### Why check future query quality when FoldBias preserves head width and works with a standard kernel? {#cross-fold-bias-compatibility-not-universal-equivalence}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Folded bias is `β(q·u)`, not always β. The mean constraint `μ·u=1` only fits the context distribution; future queries can drift. GQA head sharing compresses another object. Verify compatibility, memory, and quality separately.

    **Illustrative example:** With a future projection of 0.6, only about 60% of the original bias remains despite valid tensor shapes.

    Sources: [Folding Attention Biases into Keys Makes Compacted KV Caches Run on Standard Kernels](../../../../foundation-models/2610.36520-fold-bias/README-en.md) · [GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints](../../../../reproductions/2305.13245-gqa/README-en.md)

## Update log {#updates}

Updates record new approaches, changed trade-offs, and follow-up evidence.

**2026-10-30** · Reviewed FoldBias's constrained direction, rank-one key displacement, bf16 before value refitting, and same-value bound. Distinguished interface compatibility from structural GQA compression and retained future query drift caveats.

Affected: [Folding Attention Biases into Keys Makes Compacted KV Caches Run on Standard Kernels](../../../../foundation-models/2610.36520-fold-bias/README-en.md) · [GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints](../../../../reproductions/2305.13245-gqa/README-en.md)

**2026-10-29** · ResCom adds low-rank activation-rounding residual correction to a fixed quantized host, with host-matched calibration and intercept. HOPE assesses structured neuron pruning with Gaussian–ReLU/Hilbert proxies and compensates downstream means. Their small exact local components do not guarantee equivalent combined compression or cover LLM/ImageNet capability matrices.

Affected: [ResCom: Activation Residual Compensation for Large Language Model Quantization](../../../../foundation-models/2610.35955-rescom/README-en.md) · [Hilbert Operator for Progressive Encoding (HOPE): A Mathematical Framework for Deconstructing Learned Representations in Deep Networks](../../../../foundation-models/2607.21366-hope-hilbert/README-en.md)
